claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 accurately captures the statutory requirement from 29 CFR 825.303(a) that an employee must provide notice as soon as practicable when the timing of unforeseeable leave is not known.
Claim C0001 faithfully represents the recommendation/presumption that it generally should be practicable to give notice within the employer's usual timeframe.
Claim C0002 correctly extracts the permission permitting a spokesperson to provide notice if the employee is unable to do so personally, along with the listed illustrative options.
Claim C0003 accurately states the regulatory illustration providing an exemption from immediately leaving a child during emergency treatment for a severe asthma attack.
Claim C0004 accurately conveys the counter-example of an asthma attack handled at home requiring prompt call-in following inhaler use.
Claim C0005 correctly states the general requirement under 825.303(b) that an employee shall provide sufficient information to determine FMLA applicability.
Claim C0006 fully preserves the detailed descriptive list of types of notice content that may be required depending on the situation.
Claim C0007 correctly captures the exemption stating an employee seeking first-time FMLA leave need not expressly reference or assert the FMLA.
Claim C0008 accurately retains the requirement to specifically reference the qualifying reason or FMLA leave when seeking leave for a previously approved qualifying condition.
Claim C0009 properly states the negative rule that calling in sick alone is insufficient to trigger employer duties.
Claim C0010 faithfully reflects the expectation that the employer obtain additional information through informal means.
Claim C0011 accurately states the employee's obligation to respond to employer questions designed to assess FMLA eligibility.
Claim C0012 correctly extracts the potential consequence of denial of FMLA protection upon failure to answer reasonable employer inquiries.
Claim C0013 captures the duty under paragraph (c) to comply with employer's customary notice/procedures absent unusual circumstances.
Claim C0014 preserves the employer permission regarding calling a designated number or individual, providing surrounding context from the provision.
Claim C0015 correctly conveys the exception for an employee requiring emergency medical treatment.
Claim C0016 accurately states the rule regarding waiver of written advance notice in case of emergency FMLA leave.
Claim C0017 faithfully sets out the consequence of delay or denial when noncompliance is unjustified by unusual circumstances.
